A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same perceptual-hashing deduplication and leakage-detection study, despite changes to the title, authorship, and scope. All substantive text, equations, tables, figures, and v2 supplementary material support comparison; v1 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrowdAI duplication and leakage measurements in Table 2 and qualitative analyses of PolyWorld and HiSup predictions in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 reports dataset audits and hashing comparisons in Tables 1–4, plus original HiSup subset evaluations and duplicate-detection benchmark results in supplementary Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The DCT-based perceptual hash, exact hash matching, rotation/flip augmentation, arbitrary retention of duplicate representatives, and removal of cross-split leakage remain unchanged. v2's explicit 64-bit hash and zero Hamming-distance threshold clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 actually evaluates INRIA Aerial Image Labelling and SpaceNet 2, which v1 only mentions as background datasets. This substantially expands the audit beyond CrowdAI. CrowdAI and AICrowd refer to the same retained dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds average hashing as a comparator to perceptual hashing on official AICrowd splits (Table 4) and the constructed benchmark (Table 6). PolyWorld and HiSup remain in the qualitative comparison; other cited hashing methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include INRIA tiling into 250×250 patches, evaluation of AICrowd's separate test split, HiSup testing on seen/unseen subsets with AP and AR metrics, and a 10,000-image benchmark measuring duplicate-detection precision, recall, F1, and errors. v1's stated merging and 90%/10% repartitioning of the cleaned dataset is no longer reported.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's qualitative examples, v2 adds a quantitative seen/unseen HiSup analysis of leakage effects, controlled comparison of hashing reliability on known duplicates, and false-positive case studies for INRIA and SpaceNet. These substantially extend analysis of both downstream consequences and detector failure modes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. v2's new benchmark metrics and average runtimes do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive audit and comparison results, including HiSup AP of 79.7 on seen versus 65.4 on unseen images (Table 5), and pHash/aHash F1 scores of 0.9999/0.9429 (Table 6). The methodology's augmented-overlap count changes from 107,913 to 108,707. Exact validation-to-training leakage remains 56,368 images, or 93.45%; the new model scores are not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The DCT-and-threshold construction in v1 Algorithm 1 and Equation 1 is restated through v2 Figure 1 and its caption. No substantive mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is introduced or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions redefine the work as an audit of three geospatial datasets rather than primarily a CrowdAI investigation. The conclusion newly recommends INRIA and SpaceNet as more suitable benchmarks. The central CrowdAI contamination and overfitting claims remain, while the explicit cleaned-dataset release contribution disappears.

C2.justification: v2 explains low-contrast and no-data false positives, discusses hash sensitivity to structural differences, and interprets pHash as less prone to false positives than aHash. Its new limitations discussion acknowledges lack of inherent rotation/flip invariance and dependence on prior dataset inspection when choosing augmentations.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through explicit hash settings, AMD EPYC 7313 hardware, eight allocated cores, 32 GB memory, runtimes, dataset preparation, benchmark construction, and identification of the pretrained HiSup checkpoint. The code address changes from CrowdAI_Hash_and_search to Hash_and_search, while v1's explicit cleaned-dataset download statement is omitted; actual external availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused dataset-quality discussion with references to visual-data leakage, scale-dependent duplication, and large datasets including ImageNet, Cityscapes, VOC, and LAION-5B. The existing building-extraction and deduplication literature remains, with its detailed review condensed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Methodology and experiments gain explicit subsections, the conclusion expands into discussion and limitations, and supplementary sections are introduced. The title, author list, and dataset terminology also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the hashing pseudocode with a pipeline diagram, removes the related-work catalogue table, expands the audit tables, and adds comparison and supplementary displays. The original leakage examples are reformatted, and the PolyWorld/HiSup figure is transposed from method columns to method rows. Figures and tables are integrated more closely with the text.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on a single-dataset audit and illustrative overfitting examples. v2 addresses important validation gaps through additional dataset audits, an explicit hashing comparator and labeled benchmark, and quantitative HiSup seen/unseen evaluation, supported by implementation details and concrete limitations. Section 7's duplicate-group arithmetic is inconsistent, and the HiSup comparison does not isolate leakage as the sole cause of the performance gap. Nevertheless, the added validation substantially strengthens the paper's overall evidential quality.
